Maya (sec): quick q — we have two retention windows in play for auth/login events: SIEM indexes (30d) and long-term bucket (3y). who owns the sync/cleanup between them?
Rob (eng-infra): afaik infra writes raw events to gs://redwood-raw-logs with lifecycle rules, then a daily job ships curated events to the SIEM index. cleanup is lifecycle + index TTL.
Maya (sec): ok — two follow ups: 1) can someone confirm KMS wrapping on the archived bucket? 2) who has read access to the raw bucket for forensics?
Vivian (platform): buckets are CMEK with project CMK-prod-logs. only roles/storage.objectViewer on the bucket for tools/service accounts; humans get impersonation via access-bot timeboxed tokens.
Aaron (SRE): +1 on timeboxed tokens. we handed out short-lived GCP signed URLs for grab-and-scrub in past incidents, but that's clunky. access-bot currently creates a one-hour impersonation link and logs the grant in AuditLog.
Maya (sec): can we tighten further? ideally no direct objectViewer to humans. require a JIT workflow: ticket -> approve -> access-bot issues ephemeral grant and auto-revokes.
Rob (eng-infra): that's the plan. open question: SIEM extracts currently contain full_user_id and IP. legal asked for pseudonymization for >90d archives. do we redact before archiving or keep raw and restrict access?
Vivian (platform): tradeoffs: redacting early reduces blast radius but hurts forensic fidelity. keeping raw locked behind JIT + KMS unwrap preserves fidelity but increases access-control complexity and audit surface.
Maya (sec): preference: keep raw encrypted, enforce KMS unwrap logs + require 2-person approval for unwraps older than 180d. pseudonymize a public archive copy for analysts by default.
Aaron (SRE): ops feasibility note: adding 2-person unwrap will need integration with KMS key access logs and a workflow service. access-bot could call a small service that checks two approvers in DB and then runs gcloud kms decrypt --location=...
Rob (eng-infra): example flow draft:
1) Analyst files ticket in PagerDuty/ServiceNow with justification
2) access-bot requests primary approver from oncall rotation
3) Secondary approver (sec lead) signs off via Slack approval button
4) access-bot calls KMS/unwrap, streams objects to ephemeral staging, records audit entry with ticket id
5) After session end (TTL) files auto-delete and staging is purged
Maya (sec): love that. what about SIEM export cadence? currently exports are full delta/day. could we instead export only non-identifying events after 30d and keep deltas of raw for 90d?
Vivian (platform): we can change the transform pipeline to run a redaction step pre-export: strip user identifiers, IPs, and map to persistent pseudonyms for 90d, then wipe mapping after 180d. complexity: eval tooling expects stable pseudonyms for cross-day joins.
Aaron (SRE): also need to update alerting queries to run on pseudonymized fields — e.g., `user_pseudo_id` vs `user_id`. ops must keep backwards compatibility.
Maya (sec): audit requirements: every read of raw logs must append an evidence record in the central audit index (who, why, ticket id, KMS key version, unwrap time). can we log KMS key version?
Rob (eng-infra): yes, Cloud KMS returns keyVersion in decrypt logs. we should capture that in the audit entry. also include a hash of the object (sha256) to prove what was read.
Vivian (platform): small implementation ask: add a compact audit schema: actor, ticket_id, action, resource_path, kms_key_version, object_sha256, duration_seconds, approvers[] — store in sys-audit index with 7y retention but restricted view perms.
Maya (sec): sounds good. last piece: access-review cadence. propose quarterly review of who can approve unwraps, and monthly scan for stale service accounts with objectViewer on raw buckets.
Aaron (SRE): we can add a scheduled job that runs iam-policy-checker and opens PRs to revoke unused bindings.
Maya (sec): OK I'll draft a policy doc (retention + JIT unwrap + pseudonymization) and ping legal for the 180d threshold.
access-bot: draft ticket created: SEC-4572 — `retention/unwrap-workflow-proposal`. assigned to @Vivian and @Rob. :white_check_mark:
Rob (eng-infra): thanks — I'll prototype the access-bot unwrap flow this sprint and post a short design in #eng-infra.
Vivian (platform): I'll scope the transform pipeline changes and list required backwards-compat dependencies.
Maya (sec): thanks team. tagging this as follow-up action: SEC-4572, owners: Vivian/Rob, eta: two sprints. :lock:
